usage: This is the standard, universal way to introduce oneself across all Levantine dialects. It is used in both formal and casual settings, regardless of the speaker's gender or the listener's identity. You simply state this word followed directly by your name.

variants.label: asking a man
variants.note: Use this to ask a male for his name.

variants.label: asking a woman
variants.note: Use this to ask a female for her name.

variants.label: asking a group
variants.note: Used when addressing multiple people in Syrian and Lebanese dialects (Jordanians and Palestinians typically say 'ismkum').

variants.label: alternative introduction
variants.note: A simpler, highly common way to introduce yourself by just saying 'I am' followed by your name.

responses.english: Nice to meet you (literally: we are honored).
What a lovely name (literally: long live the names).

examples.arabic: أَنَا اِسْمِي أَحْمَد، وَإِنْتَ شُو اِسْمَك؟
examples.transliteration: ana ismi a7mad, w inte shuu ismak?
examples.english: My name is Ahmad, and what is your name?
My name is Tareq, nice to meet you.
